text.p: -- Robert Fleming Inc said it upgraded Brazilian steel firm Cosipa or Companhia Siderurgica Paulista to speculative buy from hold.
-- "One of the 45 largest steel mills in the world, Cosipa is also one of the cheapest steel stocks under several valuation criteria, with a FV/capacity of $333 per tonne," it said in a report.

-- Robert Fleming also said it believes the Administrative Economic Defense Council (Cade), Brazil's antitrust agency, will release a favorable ruling on Usiminas' 1993 acquisition of Cosipa in the next couple of months.

-- "This should make Usiminas roll out its long-hidden, aggressive strategy for Cosipa which should change the face of the steel producer and increase the speed of synergistic integration," the report said.
-- Brazilian steelmaker Usiminas owns a 25 percent stake in Cosipa's total capital.
-- It added that, if the Cade gives Usiminas the green light, Cosipa's share could skyrocket after a 57 percent decline year-to-date.
-- Cosipa preferred shares traded at 0.67 reais, up 4.68 percent from Monday's close, at 1620 local time/1920 GMT on the Sao Paulo bourse.
